title: GET /api/format answers with the product's reference as JSON
statement: The response MUST be 200 with `content-type: application/json` and the `FormatReference` that `formatReference` builds for the product root, extensions included.

title: GET /api/history reads git safely for the record's own rows
statement: The endpoint MUST find the data file that holds the record's row from the data by the record's ID and MUST answer 404 (`no-record`) for an ID no record has, never reading a path from the request. It MUST answer 400 for a missing ID, a negative `skip`, or a `commit` that is not a hex hash of 4 to 40 characters or `working`. It MUST run git with argument arrays, never through a shell, inside the product root, with no optional locks or prompts, stopped after a time limit and cut at an output cap (the answer says `truncated`). The list MUST hold the commits that changed the record's rows, newest first, twenty a page with `more`, and the changes the working tree holds that are not committed yet. A folder that is not a git repository, or a machine without git, MUST answer 200 with `no-repo` and a calm message. Answers carry `cache-control: no-store`.

title: Steps are shown in their positions, as numbers
statement: A flow's steps MUST be shown in their `position`, compared as numbers (so step 10 comes after step 2), then by ID; the store refuses a step without a whole-number position, so none is ever hidden.

title: A step is always shown under its flow
statement: Wherever steps are shown, on a page or in the graph, each MUST be shown under the flow it belongs to, never as a record apart from it.

title: A step that fulfills a rule is traced with its flow
statement: Where a flow step fulfills a requirement or rule, the trace MUST show the step's flow too, so the rule is traced to the flow through the step.

title: Every record ID shown is a link to that record
statement: Wherever a page shows a record ID, it MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to that record's page, so any reference can be followed or opened in a new tab.

title: A wiki page shows one level below its record by default
statement: A wiki page (product, domain, record or group) and the side bar MUST show by default only the records one level below the page's own record. Anything deeper MUST be folded under its row and open only when the person opens it, opens everything, or searches for something inside it.

title: A folded row keeps its count and its marks
statement: A folded row MUST still show how many records it holds ("4 requirements") and its own coverage marks and problem badge, so nothing hidden is forgotten.

title: A record ID named in text is a link in the text, never a relation
statement: A record ID named in a text field MUST be shown only as a link in the text: it MUST NOT appear among the record's links out or in, in the graph, or in coverage.

title: Code and links in text are shown as written
statement: Turning named IDs into links MUST NOT change text inside code blocks, links the author wrote, or code spans holding anything besides one ID; a code span holding one lone record ID is wrapped in the link with its code style kept, and it MUST run only on the sanitized HTML.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link to it
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST hold exactly one link that stands for the whole row, and that link MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to the record's page, so the row can be followed or opened in a new tab like any other reference. Other links in the row lead elsewhere and stay links of their own.

title: Links are shown by their labels, never by relation codes
statement: Wherever a page names a link, as a heading, a list title, a field label, an edge label or a tooltip, it MUST use the relation rule's `forward_label` read from the link's source or its `reverse_label` read from its target. A relation code such as `satisfies` or `proves` MUST NOT be shown as a heading or label; it may appear only as code, where a page explains how to write a link.

title: GET /api/spec answers with the product's data, labeled when it is the fixture
statement: The response MUST be 200 with the product's data as the store loads it and the checks find it, and MUST NOT be cached. When the sample fixture is served instead, because `LATHE_SPEC_FIXTURE=1` is set or the engine cannot load, the response MUST carry `x-lathe-source: fixture` and the reason in `x-lathe-source-reason`.

title: POST /api/write answers the changed rows, or the refusal with its reasons
statement: A write the store accepts MUST answer 200 with `ok: true`, the tables and files it changed and each changed row before and after; a write the store refuses MUST answer 422 with `ok: false`, a sentence and every store problem with its command index, and MUST change no file.

title: POST /api/write refuses what is not a write from the app
statement: The endpoint MUST answer 405 to any method but POST, 403 to a request from another site, 415 to a body that is not `application/json`, 413 to a body over 1 MB, and 400 to a body that is not `{ commands }` with 1 to 500 commands of a known shape, each with a sentence and no write.
